sections.overview: This sphinx moth is common in tropical and subtropical America and occurs less often in southern Florida.
sections.identification: Adults are mostly grey-brown; the large caterpillars are conspicuous, with black-and-yellow rings and a reddish head.
sections.habitat: Caterpillars often occur in gardens on frangipani and related host plants.
sections.diet: Larvae feed on Apocynaceae leaves; adults visit flowers for nectar.
sections.behavior: Adults are active at night and attracted to lights.
sections.reproduction: Females lay about 50–100 eggs in clusters on host-plant leaves.
sections.ecology: Its bold larval colors are described as a warning signal, although some predators still eat the caterpillars.
